Byomkesh.description: The protagonist and renowned detective who prefers the title 'Truth Seeker', investigating the mystery at Chorabali Estate.

Ajit.description: Ajit is the narrator and close friend of Byomkesh, who accompanies him on his cases and documents their adventures.

Kumar Tridib.description: A friend of Byomkesh and Ajit, owner of an estate near Chorabali, who invites them for a holiday and becomes involved in the case.

Himangshu.description: The zaminder (landlord) of Chorabali Estate and an avid hunter who hosts the investigation.

Kaligati Bhattacharjee.description: The Dewan (manager) of Chorabali Estate and a devout worshipper of Kali who manages the estate's finances.

Baby.description: Himangshu's young daughter, who is fond of her tutor and becomes friendly with Byomkesh and Ajit.

Harinath Choudhary.description: The missing tutor of Baby whose mysterious disappearance is the central focus of the story.

Anadi Sarkar.description: The head servant of the estate, an old and loyal employee whose family becomes entangled in the household's troubles.

Radha.description: Anadi Sarkar's widowed daughter, who faces social stigma and personal tragedy.

Bhuban.description: Himangshu's personal bearer, who provides information about Harinath and the household.

Chorabali.description: The name of Himangshu's estate, meaning 'quicksand' in Bengali, named after a dangerous sandy patch on the property.

Calcutta.description: A major city in India (now Kolkata), the home city of Byomkesh and Ajit.

Sir Digindra.description: Kumar Tridib's uncle, mentioned in connection with a previous story, 'Hidden Heirloom'.

Tripura.description: A region in northeast India, referenced as a destination for a hunting expedition.

B.Sc..description: Bachelor of Science, an academic degree mentioned as Harinath's qualification.

Kali.description: A Hindu goddess, worshipped by Kaligati and referenced in the tutor's spiritual practices.

Benares.description: A city in India (now Varanasi), mentioned as the destination where Radha is sent.

Registry Office.description: A government office where property deeds and legal documents are registered.

North Bengal.description: A region in the state of West Bengal, India, where Chorabali Estate is located.

babu.description: A respectful term of address for a gentleman, often used in Bengal.

puja.description: A Hindu religious ritual or worship ceremony.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment for men, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia.

kameej.description: A tunic or long shirt, commonly worn in South Asia.

tika.description: A mark, often red, worn on the forehead as a religious symbol.

Rudraksha.description: A sacred seed often used for prayer beads in Hinduism, associated with Lord Shiva.

asana.description: A posture or seat, especially in the context of meditation or yoga.

almanac.description: A calendar or annual publication containing important dates and astronomical information, used here to determine lunar phases.

didi.description: An affectionate term for an elder sister or respected woman.

dada.description: An affectionate term for an elder brother or respected man.

sadhu.description: A holy man or ascetic in Hindu tradition.

mantra.description: A sacred utterance or chant, often used in spiritual practices.

hymn.description: A religious song or chant, here referring to a prayer to goddess Kali.

bearer.description: A personal attendant or servant, especially one who serves food or performs household duties.
